item.title: See Full List Of NDC Campaign Council Members
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) on Sunday released the list of its newly constituted national campaign council for the 2027 general elections. The list has Senator Seriake Dickson as the chairman, while the presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, were listed as co-chairman and co-vice chairman of the national campaign council, respectively. Others are Senator Cleopas Zuwoghe as vice chairman, and former secretary to the government of the federation, Babachir Lawal (National Campaign Advisory Council), as a member. Also on the list are Ikenna Enekweizu, Sidi Abdul, Babatunde Alli, Senator Ovie Omo Agege, Senator Victor Umeh, Ibrahim Abdulkarim (DG, Presidential Campaign), Buba Galadima, Yakubu Ochefu, Mahmud Jahun, Moshood Salvador, Mrs. Dudu Manuga, Victor Ogene, and Muktar Usman. The list also has a 40-member national campaign advisory council and 37 state campaign coordinators. The NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, was named Director of Communication and Media. A former defence spokesperson, Major General John Enenche (retd.), was named Director of Security and Intelligence. The party, in a statement announcing the campaign council on its X handle, said, “The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) is pleased to announce the constitution of its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections. “The National Campaign Council will provide strategic leadership, coordinate campaign activities across the country, and drive the mobilisation of Nigerians behind the party’s vision of a new, just, and prosperous Nigeria. “The Council will work under the chairmanship of His Excellency, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson CON, NDC National Leader; Co-Chairman, His Excellency, Mr. Peter Obi CON, our presidential candidate; Vice Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, NDC National Chairman and our vice-presidential candidate, His Excellency, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, Co Vice-Chairman, Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu, NDC National Secretary, Council Secretary, and the Director-General, Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim to deliver a people-centred and issue-based campaign. “We call on all party members, supporters, and well-meaning Nigerians to remain united and focused as we work together to rescue our country.” See Full List Below: The post See Full List Of NDC Campaign Council Members appeared first on Channels Television .

No candidate who lost the first round has gone on to win the second in Brazil since 1989, the first direct election after the end of the country’s military dictatorship. “People went to vote because we managed to convince them that voting was very important for ensuring democracy in the country,” Lula said in his first comments after the win. Fireworks and vuvuzelas rang out in Rio de Janeiro, while thousands of people dressed in red, the color of Lula’s Workers’ Party, streamed into the streets of Sao Paulo to celebrate. Lula’s Fight Back After the first-round defeat, the left swung into action with massive rallies, declaring “Never Again Bolsonaro” and revamped their social media strategy. The abstention rate decreased from the first round, falling from 21 percent to 19 percent. Julio Canelo, 42, a lawyer celebrating in Rio de Janeiro, hailed a victory for “the entire democratic spectrum.” “It was the result of the people mobilizing, in the streets and online,” he told AFP. A fierce social media battle drew in Meta, parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, which Lula’s campaign accused of favoring his opponent with “algorithmic manipulation.” Meta denied this but acknowledged that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors. “We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula said of social media companies after his win. A bitter campaign marred by scandals and mudslinging laid bare the deep divisions that have plagued Brazil over the past decade. Brazil’s right-wing senator and presidential candidate for the Liberal Party (PL) Flavio Bolsonaro reacts after knowing the first results in the presidential runoff election, in Brasilia, on October 25, 2026. A Country Split In Two Lula heads into a fourth term with almost half of the nation having rejected him, desperate for change. He rose from poverty to become president in 2003 and was re-elected in 2006. Lula made a dramatic return to office in the 2022 elections after a corruption scandal saw him jailed for over 18 months. The charges were annulled on procedural grounds. In his third term, Lula oversaw a drop in inflation and unemployment, and lifted millions out of hunger, but many voters felt gloomy about the high cost of living and crime. Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, pitched himself as more moderate and jovial than his father and managed to galvanize conservatives as well as less ideological voters wanting something new. “We’re in a deep hole, things are dire. People can barely afford to eat — buying meat is out of the question,” said Tereza Cristina Ramos, a 68-year-old retiree, who voted in Rio de Janeiro. Already one of the world’s oldest leaders, Lula will be 85 by the end of his new term in 2030. He is also facing a hostile Congress dominated by the right. Lula’s campaign leaned heavily on the theme of sovereignty in the face of commercial and diplomatic pressure from Trump’s United States. “This country will not accept being anyone’s backyard,” he said Sunday. Lula received congratulations from Chile’s far-right president, Jose Antonio Kast, and Ecuador’s right-wing Daniel Noboa — both close Trump allies. item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, Chairman, Board of Directors of DAAR Communications Plc, Raymond Dokpesi Jnr and President of the Nigeria Institute of Public Relations, NIPR, Dr. Ike Neliaku, have called for a new partnership between government, media and citizens to deepen democracy and honour late media icon, High Chief Raymond Dokpesi. They spoke on Sunday in Abuja at the 3rd Raymond Dokpesi Annual Diamond Lecture themed “Media, Democratic Consolidation and Development.” Uzodimma set the tone, urging government at all levels to stop treating the media as detractors or enemies. “Going forward, I propose a three-way pact between government, the media, and the citizens that will enable the media to drive national development,” he said. The media profession must also defend that freedom through the quality of its work,” Uzodimma said. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 26, 2026
item.description: The dollar is trading at different rates against the naira across Nigeria’s official foreign exchange market and the parallel market on Monday, October 26, 2026, with the latest available quotations showing differences between the two segments. At the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the official exchange rate was around ₦1,331 per dollar in the latest available market update, while parallel-market dealers quoted rates of approximately ₦1,370 to ₦1,385 per dollar, depending on the location and transaction. Data published by Gatekeepers News on Monday put the official dollar selling rate at ₦1,331.28, while the parallel market recorded a buying rate of ₦1,370 and a selling rate of ₦1,385 per dollar. However, exchange rates vary among banks, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators and other currency dealers, and the actual rate available to customers may differ from published indicative figures. The official foreign exchange market remains a key source of dollar pricing for eligible transactions conducted through authorised channels. The latest available figures for October 26 put the dollar at approximately ₦1,331 per dollar in the official market. This compares with the parallel market, where customers may pay more to purchase physical dollars. International currency data also showed movements in the dollar-naira pair on Monday, although such reference rates do not necessarily match the Central Bank of Nigeria’s official NFEM rate or the rates offered by local currency dealers. In the parallel market, currency dealers were quoting the dollar at approximately ₦1,370 for buying and ₦1,385 for selling, according to the latest market update published on Monday. The buying rate represents the amount dealers pay customers selling dollars, while the selling rate is the amount customers pay when purchasing the US currency. Based on these indicative quotations, $100 would be worth about ₦137,000 when sold to a dealer at the buying rate. Someone purchasing $100 at the selling rate would pay approximately ₦138,500. For $500, the equivalent would be ₦685,000 at the buying rate and ₦692,500 at the selling rate. Meanwhile, $1,000 would exchange for approximately ₦1,370,000 when sold to a dealer or cost ₦1,385,000 to purchase. These calculations are estimates based on published rates. Actual transactions may differ according to dealer pricing, location, dollar availability and the amount exchanged. Movements in the dollar-to-naira exchange rate affect Nigerian businesses and households that depend on imported goods and international payments. A higher dollar rate can increase the naira cost of imported raw materials, machinery, electronics and other products. Importers may consequently face higher operating expenses, which can feed into retail prices. Nigerians paying overseas tuition fees, medical bills and travel expenses also monitor exchange rates because changes in the value of the naira affect how much they need to pay for dollar-denominated transactions

item.description: By Efe Onodjae Social media has been awash with reactions following the display of brand-new Toyota Prado SUVs by the National Youth Leader of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dayo Israel, for selected youth leaders of the party. Israel, in a post on X on Sunday, said the 2026 Prado SUVs were presented to support the beneficiaries’ election mobilisation activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also expressed appreciation to First Lady Oluremi Tinubu for her support for the party’s youth structure. However, the announcement, accompanied by a video showing seven vehicles, sparked criticism from Nigerians, with many questioning the timing of the gesture amid the economic hardship confronting citizens. Some users also questioned the source of funding for the vehicles, while others compared the expenditure with the challenges facing the country’s healthcare sector and security personnel. item.title: Nigeria must manufacture meters locally, secure sustainable financing — Experts
item.description: By Esther Ihejirika Electricity sector experts have called for increased local meter manufacturing, sustainable financing and wider adoption of smart technology to accelerate meter deployment and close Nigeria’s metering gap. They made the call during a webinar on rapid meter rollout, stressing the need for a coordinated national metering plan to improve revenue collection, reduce estimated billing and curb electricity theft. Mr. Odion Omonfoman, host of the webinar, disclosed that the company had achieved “over 90 per cent metering coverage” and deployed more than 200,000 meters through the Meter Asset Provider (MAP) scheme and vendor-financing model. item.title: Domestic crude supply to refineries declines 6.3% to 15.97mb —NMDPRA
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa Domestic crude oil supply to Nigerian refineries declined by 6.3 per cent to 15.97 million barrels in September 2026 from 17.05 million barrels in August. This comes as petrol supply from domestic refineries and imports fell sharply during the month. The September 2026 Midstream and Downstream Report released by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) on Thursday shows that the decline in crude supply coincided with a 23.4 per cent drop in average daily petrol supply to 38.7 million litres from 50.5 million litres in August. The report attributed the fall in petrol receipts to lower domestic supply and reduced imports as approved import permit volumes were being exhausted. Between January and September 2026, refineries received a combined 156.51 million barrels of crude oil, comprising 125.85 million barrels of domestic crude and 30.66 million barrels of imported crude. Domestic production accounted for 80.4 per cent of total intake, while imported cargoes contributed 19.6 per cent. The report further showed that Dangote Refinery’s utilisation stood at 105.98 per cent in September, implying crude processing of approximately 689,000 barrels per day against average crude receipts of 618,000 barrels per day. The difference of about 71,000 barrels per day was drawn from refinery inventory, indicating that the refinery processed more crude than it received during the month. Despite the September decline, domestic refineries remained the larger source of petrol supply, accounting for approximately 73.6 per cent of total receipts during the month, compared with 26.4 per cent from imports. The September total was also below the 13-month average of 49.7 million litres per day recorded between September 2025 and September 2026. Over the 13-month period, domestic refineries supplied an average of 30.4 million litres per day, accounting for 61.2 per cent of total supply, while imports contributed 19.3 million litres per day, or 38.8 per cent. The NMDPRA said September petrol receipts declined as domestic supply fell 21 per cent below August levels, while imports dropped by 30 per cent amid the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes. item.title: Stock market extend losses, 55 stocks depreciate
item.description: …As 20 record capital gains By Peter Egwuatu Share prices of 55 companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) depreciated last week following profit taking by the investors. However, 20 stocks appreciated in price during the week under review. The week’s performance highlights the market correction facing the stock market as investors reassess their portfolios following the substantial gains recorded earlier in the year. Although selected stocks attracted buying interest, the recovery was not broad enough to offset losses in influential stocks, leaving the overall market sentiment negative. Analysts emphasised that the decline also came against the backdrop of rising international oil prices, which climbed sharply amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. While higher crude prices could support Nigeria’s export earnings and government revenue, their broader implications for domestic fuel costs, inflation and business expenses remain important considerations for investors. A review of the market performance last week showed that the NGX market capitalisation, which represents the total value of stocks, shed over N206 billion to close at N160.519 trillion from N160.725 trillion the previous week. In similar manner, the NGX All Share Index, ASI, close lower to 247,222.27 points from 247539.73 points. Meanwhile, a total turnover of 2.024 billion shares worth N110.773 billion in 173,113 deals was traded last week by investors on the floor of the Exchange, in contrast to a total of 1.659 billion shares valued at N98.088 billion that exchanged hands the previous week in 184,632 deals. The Financial Services Industry (measured by volume) led the activity chart with 1.111 billion shares valued at N53.908 billion traded in 81,787 deals: thus contributing 54.89% and 48.66% to the total equity turnover volume and value respectively. The Consumer Goods Industry followed with 394.039 million shares worth N9.811 billion in 17,912 deals. Third place was the Agriculture Industry, with a turnover of 147.170 million shares worth N2.821 billion in 7,462 deals. Analysing market performance and outlook, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, stated: “The near-term outlook for the Nigerian equities market remains cautious as investors balance the need to preserve gains against opportunities in selected stocks. The market’s substantial year-to-date appreciation provides important context for the recent weakness, as some participants may be reducing exposure after the strong returns accumulated earlier in the year. Continued selling pressure in banking, energy and other influential stocks could prolong the market’s consolidation. Further weakness in large capitalised stocks may continue to weigh on the benchmark even if selected equities record positive returns.” The post Stock market extend losses, 55 stocks depreciate appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Soldiers earn peanuts, APC youth leader flaunts billion-naira SUVs — Utomi
item.description: Professor Pat Utomi has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) over the distribution of luxury sport utility vehicles (SUVs) to selected youth leaders, contrasting the expenditure with what he described as poor salaries paid to Nigerian soldiers. Utomi, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), said it was troubling that an APC youth leader could display expensive vehicles at a time Nigerians had been told that government funds were limited. In a post on X on Sunday, Utomi wrote: “Nigerian soldiers are being paid peanuts as salaries, yet an APC youth leader is flaunting SUVs worth billions of naira. This is the same government that told Nigerians there was no longer money in the treasury. At this point, they must think we are fools!” In another post, the professor questioned whether the money spent on the vehicles could have been put to better use, particularly in the health sector. “Each of the SUVs in this video costs more than ₦100 million. I wonder how many world-class ambulances the millions being spent on these vehicles could buy. What a pity!” he wrote. The comments followed a video posted by APC National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, showing brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado SUVs he said were presented to selected youth leaders to support election mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Today, I presented brand new 2026 Prado to my committed selected youth leaders to aid their election mobilisation activities,” Israel wrote. He also expressed gratitude to First Lady Oluremi Tinubu for what he described as her continued support for the party’s structure under his leadership. “The party is supreme and that supremacy will show in our action in this election period — we will deliver polling unit by polling unit,” he added. The video, which has since been deleted, drew criticism from Nigerians on social media, with some questioning the timing of the vehicle distribution amid the economic hardship associated with the Tinubu administration’s reforms. Utomi’s remarks add to the criticism surrounding the display, with the NDC chieftain raising questions about public spending priorities and the cost of the vehicles. item.title: IPoB alleges secret transfer of 68 detainees
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—The Indigenous People of Biafra, IPoB, has alleged that 68 detained Biafrans were secretly transferred from Wawa Barracks to correctional facilities in Kuje, Keffi and Suleja, accusing the Federal Government of using the justice system to prolong the detention of its members. The group also alleged that the Court of Appeal had yet to list an appeal challenging the conviction of its leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, despite the compilation and transmission of the record of appeal. IPOB made the allegations in its weekly address issued on Sunday by the Head of its Directorate of State, DOS, Mazi Chris Nwaogu. Nwaogu said the group’s legal team had identified the 68 detainees and was working to secure their release. He urged supporters to sustain legal efforts on behalf of those in custody. He further alleged that a separate fundamental rights suit concerning Kanu’s detention had suffered a setback after the presiding judge reportedly announced that the court file was missing. item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Share prices of 55 companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) depreciated last week following profit taking by the investors. However, 20 stocks appreciated in price during the week under review. The week’s performance highlights the market correction facing the stock market as investors reassess their portfolios following the substantial gains recorded earlier in the year. Although selected stocks attracted buying interest, the recovery was not broad enough to offset losses in influential stocks, leaving the overall market sentiment negative. Analysts emphasised that the decline also came against the backdrop of rising international oil prices, which climbed sharply amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. While higher crude prices could support Nigeria’s export earnings and government revenue, their broader implications for domestic fuel costs, inflation and business expenses remain important considerations for investors. A review of the market performance last week showed that the NGX market capitalisation, which represents the total value of stocks, shed over N206 billion to close at N160.519 trillion from N160.725 trillion the previous week. In similar manner, the NGX All Share Index, ASI, close lower to 247,222.27 points from 247539.73 points. Meanwhile, a total turnover of 2.024 billion shares worth N110.773 billion in 173,113 deals was traded last week by investors on the floor of the Exchange, in contrast to a total of 1.659 billion shares valued at N98.088 billion that exchanged hands the previous week in 184,632 deals. The Financial Services Industry (measured by volume) led the activity chart with 1.111 billion shares valued at N53.908 billion traded in 81,787 deals: thus contributing 54.89% and 48.66% to the total equity turnover volume and value respectively. The Consumer Goods Industry followed with 394.039 million shares worth N9.811 billion in 17,912 deals. Third place was the Agriculture Industry, with a turnover of 147.170 million shares worth N2.821 billion in 7,462 deals. Analysing market performance and outlook, analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, stated: “The near-term outlook for the Nigerian equities market remains cautious as investors balance the need to preserve gains against opportunities in selected stocks. The market’s substantial year-to-date appreciation provides important context for the recent weakness, as some participants may be reducing exposure after the strong returns accumulated earlier in the year. Continued selling pressure in banking, energy and other influential stocks could prolong the market’s consolidation. Further weakness in large capitalised stocks may continue to weigh on the benchmark even if selected equities record positive returns.” Vanguard News The post Stock market extend losses, 55 stocks depreciate; 20 record capital gains appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Death toll in Taraba bandits’ attack now 50
item.description: The death toll from an attack by gunmen in Taraba State has risen to at least 50, survivors and Amnesty International told AFP Sunday, after more bodies were discovered. Read Also: ‘We counted over 20 bodies after attackers left’ – Taraba massacre survivors Both police and Amnesty said some of the victims had drowned while trying to flee the attackers. Gunmen on motorcycles from a suspected “bandit” gang swarmed Binnari, in eastern Taraba, killing dozens of people shortly after Friday prayers. They also looted and burned stores. Taraba is sandwiched between northeastern Nigeria, which has a long-running jihadist insurgency, and the volatile central region, which faces criminal gangs known as bandits. Driven by money rather than ideology, the bandits in Nigeria target poorly policed rural areas, kidnapping for ransom and killing. “On Friday, we found seven bodies after the bandits attacked our community,” said Bashir Mamuda Musa, a resident of Binnari, in Taraba state. “The following day, Saturday, we discovered another 43 bodies in the river, bringing the total to 50,” he added. The new toll was confirmed by resident Abdullahi Zakari. “Many residents, including women and children, fled towards the river in an attempt to escape the gunmen,” Zakari told AFP. “Unfortunately, several people drowned while trying to flee the attack.” ‘Chased into river’ Bodies can often be difficult to recover when communities scatter. Some were discovered in a nearby river, according to both police and Amnesty. Police spokesman for the state Victor Msheliza told AFP on Sunday that they were still searching the area. Officers “found some (bodies) in the river” of people who were trying to escape, he said. Police were immediately deployed to the area after the attack, more deployments being sent, he said. Amnesty International gave a toll of 52 on Sunday, saying the attackers had come “in large numbers and set ablaze shops and market stalls”. “The bandits invaded in large numbers,… chased people and they headed toward the river to escape,” and drowned, Amnesty International Nigeria director Isa Sanusi told AFP. “Some were chased into the river by the gunmen”. Banditry has become a growing problem in northwest and central Nigeria, with powerful gangs battling overstretched police and military across hard-to-reach, rural locations. They raid villages and impose “taxes” on farmers and mining operations in areas with little state presence. Amnesty, in a post on X, blamed the Nigerian authorities for leaving some rural communities “at the mercy of gunmen that repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity. “Consistent failure of the authorities to bring the suspected perpetrators to justice is clearly emboldening impunity,” the rights group said on social media. item.title: Kane primed to beat Yamal, Mbappe to Ballon d’Or glory
item.description: England captain Harry Kane is the favourite to win a wide open race to be crowned Ballon d’Or winner at a glitzy London ceremony on Monday, with Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe also in the running to be named the world’s best footballer. Read Also: 2026 Ballon d’or ceremony: date, time and how to watch The 70th edition of the award, established by the magazine France Football, will be hosted in England for the first time in recognition of the first winner Stanley Matthews and fittingly could have a first English winner for 25 years. Bayern Munich striker Kane struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, leading the German giants to a league and cup double and England to the semi-finals of the World Cup. “I’d love to be able to achieve something like that. I would be a massive milestone in my career,” said the 33-year-old. But semi-final exits in both the Champions League and World Cup for Kane means the outcome is far from certain. “I think my wife would prefer to know and my family … it’s very stressful for everyone,” he added. “I can see why they don’t tell people. They want everyone to go, all the big names, and there will be more people watching it if they don’t know.” ‘I deserve it’ Yamal finished second to Paris Saint-Germain’s Ousmane Dembele last year and the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar seems destined to be a Ballon d’Or winner one day. However, after a hamstring injury ended his club season early, he was far from the shining light of Spain’s World Cup triumph that was built on being the best collective unit. Yamal was pipped to both the player and young player of the tournament by his Barcelona team-mates Rodri and Pau Cubarsi. That has not diminished his bullish confidence ahead of the ceremony. “For me, Mbappe and me, we’re the two best players in the world,” Yamal said last month. “I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I’ve won.” Mbappe, by contrast, boasts plenty of personal milestones without medals for either Real Madrid or France. The 27-year-old was top goalscorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup without winning any of those trophies. His 10 World Cup goals made him the top goalscorer in the competition’s history on 22. “Being the all-time top scorer in World Cup history, overtaking all the great legends in the history of the sport in the most important tournament there is, is something that really stands out,” said Mbappe. “Who am I voting for? Myself.” One football journalist from each of the 100 top nations in FIFA’s rankings is invited to cast votes for their top 10 players from a 30-man shortlist, allocating a maximum of 15 points down to one based on their ranking. The Ballon d’Or goes to the player who accrued the most points. Although the award carries no cash prize, it can generate huge bonuses from clubs and commercial partners as well as increasing a player’s overall marketing value.

item.title: MENOPAUSE: Women urged to seek care, manage symptoms early
item.description: Platform bringing together women, healthcare professionals, policy makers, corporate organisations, wellness practitioners and community stakeholders, Menopause West Africa, has warned that menopause symptoms could be fatal if not properly managed, saying although menopause is not a disease, issues affecting women should be treated with concern because of their unique role in society. Chairman of the Organising Committee of Menopause West Africa, Mr Clifford Okwesi, said no fewer than 100 women had been commissioned as mentors, adding that plans were underway to reach 3,000 churches and other places of worship across the country. Okwesi spoke during the induction of no fewer than 100 women as mentors at the 2026 edition of Menopause West Africa, themed, ‘Advancing the Conversation on Women’s Health, Well-Being and Institutional Support’, held in Lagos and sponsored by Menofix Herbals capsule. Also speaking at the event, veteran Nollywood actress, Patience Ozokwor, said menopause was not a disease but a stage in every woman’s life. She charged the mentors, also known as Menopause Champions, to reach out to grassroots communities and educate younger women who had not yet reached that stage of life on how to ensure a smooth transition. The actress called on women in positions of authority to support other women on the subject and empower them meaningfully, rather than limiting such support to their relatives. According to her, by empowering more women would reduce family burdens, which often rested on women. She advised women to watch their diets, exercise regularly and, most importantly, visit hospitals at regular intervals to monitor their health and make necessary adjustments. She said: “Do things that will help your body. Get up, walk around and don’t eat all the time.” Meanwhile, President of the Association of West African Society of Obstetrics and Gynaecologists, AWASOG, Professor Brian Adinma, said menopause marked a significant stage in a woman’s reproductive life and represented a new beginning that required knowledge, preparation and care. The medical expert discussed several aspects of menopause, including its types, stages, symptoms and management procedures, before answering questions from participants. For her part, President of the Customs Officers’ Wives Association, COWA, Mrs Kikilomo Adeniyi, said menopause was not the end of womanhood but a new chapter in life that required strength, wisdom and renewed purpose. Represented by the President of COWA’s Tin Can Island Chapter, Mrs Caroline Ifeoluwa, Adeniyi said the health, welfare and empowerment of women remained central to the association’s vision, adding that a healthy woman built a stronger family. Justice, in the sense Sule meant it, is broader than court judgments or legal technicalities. It includes fair representation, equitable distribution of public resources, respect for the rule of law, protection of minorities, credible elections and equal treatment before public institutions. It means that a farmer in Zamfara, a trader in Onitsha, a teacher in Lagos, a fisherman in Bayelsa and a herder in Sokoto should all be able to expect the state to protect their lives, respect their rights and respond to their needs without discrimination. Sule put it plainly: “If you do justice to all and sundry — and I say all and sundry — because Allah says, ‘If you are going to judge between two people, do justice irrespective of the tribe, religion or even political inclination; justice must be done to whosoever deserves it.’” That standard is demanding. It rejects the politics of “our turn” when it becomes a cover for exclusion. It also rejects the politics of revenge, where one group’s victory is treated as another group’s defeat. Nigeria needs leaders who can rise above such thinking. The late Dan Masanin Kano was equally clear that justice must not be selective. “I am not asking you — and I know you will not — to discriminate against any part of Nigeria,” he told Buhari. “But I am asking you to do justice to all parts of Nigeria.” For political parties preparing for 2027, fairness must begin before the first ballot is cast. It must be visible in candidate selection, zoning arrangements, internal party democracy, campaign financing and the treatment of aspirants. When parties manipulate primaries, impose candidates, marginalise women and young people, or allow money to determine nomination, they weaken the legitimacy of the eventual winner. A flawed process produces a fragile mandate. And a fragile mandate makes governing harder, especially in a country where citizens are already sceptical of political promises. Fairness also requires issue-based campaigns. Nigeria’s problems are real: insecurity, unemployment, inflation, poor infrastructure, weak public services, climate pressure on agriculture and widespread poverty. These challenges do not respect ethnicity or religion. Candidates should therefore be judged on their plans to secure communities, create jobs, reform institutions, expand opportunities and restore public confidence. A campaign built on fear, sectional resentment or religious division may win attention, but it cannot build a nation. Sule’s warning remains urgent: force, fear and power cannot govern the mind or conquer the spirit. Only justice and fair play can. Sule linked justice directly to peace and development. “Justice will bring about peace,” he said. “Peace and stability are the pre-requisites of development.” No society develops sustainably in an atmosphere of fear. Investors hesitate where contracts are uncertain and violence is common. Farmers abandon land where insecurity prevails. Young people lose hope where merit is ignored and corruption rewards the connected. Communities retreat into distrust when they believe the state protects some citizens more than others. Peace is not merely the absence of gunfire. It is the presence of confidence: confidence that elections will count, that courts will be impartial, that public offices will serve the public, and that no region, faith or class will be permanently shut out of opportunity. The 2027 election offers Nigeria a chance to rebuild that confidence. But it will require more than campaign rhetoric. It will require electoral institutions that are visibly independent, security agencies that act professionally, political actors who accept results peacefully, and citizens who refuse to be used as instruments of violence. Nigeria does not lack talent, resources or ideas. What it often lacks is the disciplined commitment to justice that turns diversity into strength rather than division. Justice is the key.” If Nigeria’s political class embraces that key, the 2027 election can become more than another contest for office. It can become a renewal of the national promise—a step towards a country at peace with itself, fair to all its people, and capable at last of fulfilling its vast potential. •Ogbeifun wrote in from Lagos. item.title: Opebi-Mende-Ojota Link Bridge To Be Opened Before Christmas, Says Sanwo-Olu
item.description: The Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has said that the Opebi-Mende Link Bridge is about 80 per cent complete, expressing confidence that the project will be opened to the public before Christmas. Governor Sanwo-Olu gave the assurance during an inspection of the project, acknowledging that the construction had exceeded the September completion timeline previously announced. He said his visit to the site was to establish the reasons for the delay and assess the progress of work, stressing that the project’s distinctive architectural design and engineering requirements must not be compromised by the pressure to meet the deadline. He explained that the bridge’s steel structure was designed to reflect the area’s historical association with cane weaving, thereby preserving its cultural identity. According to him, the project involves installing more than 300 tonnes of steel at heights of up to 25 metres, making it an unusually demanding engineering undertaking. The governor said three of the four major steel components, designed to resemble interwoven cane, had been completed, while work was ongoing on the remaining component. He added that light-emitting diode (LED) installations featuring the colours of Lagos State would enhance the structure and give it an iconic appearance. Governor Sanwo-Olu added that the state government would not sacrifice engineering quality and public safety for speed, despite the delay. He said additional activities, including site cleaning, repainting of kerbs, restoration of affected areas and landscaping, would be undertaken before the bridge is opened to the public. He envisaged the area becoming a destination for recreation, cultural heritage and tourism, adding that its redevelopment would enable residents to appreciate the history and identity of the community. The governor maintained that the bridge would become a significant infrastructure landmark in Lagos, combining innovation with cultural preservation. Sanwo-Olu commissioned the construction of the bridge in 2022 to ease congestion in Ikeja and environs. Governor Sanwo-Olu (centre) He said that the bridge, which is part of the ‘legacy project,’ was an innovative solution to the perennial gridlock around Opebi/Mobolaji Bank Anthony Way/Ojota/Mende corridor. item.title: Were Young People Removed From Nigeria’s Voter Register?
item.description: The recent voter registration figures released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) have raised important questions about the declining number of young people on Nigeria’s voter register. Let’s look at what the data tells us. According to INEC, Nigeria had 93,469,008 registered voters in 2023, distributed across four age categories: • Youth: 18–34 years: 37,060,399 (39.6 per cent) • Middle age: 35–49 years: 33,413,591 (35.8 per cent) • Elderly: 50–69 years: 17,700,270 (18.9 per cent) • 70 years and above: 5,294,748 (5.7 per cent) The 2026 figures show that the voter register has increased to 103,428,715 registered voters, representing an increase of 9,959,707 voters, and representing 10.66 per cent compared with the 11.27 per cent increase recorded in 2023. The 2026 age distribution is as follows: • Youth: 18–34 years: 29,777,578 (28.79 per cent) • Middle age: 35–49 years: 43,265,946 (41.83 per cent) • Elderly: 50–69 years: 22,982,900 (22.22 per cent) • 70 years and above: 7,402,291 (7.16 per cent) What Do These Figures Tell Us? 1. While the overall voter register figure for 2026 increased by 10.66 per cent, the number of registered voters aged 18–34 declined by 7,282,821, representing a 19.65 per cent reduction in this age category. Their share of the register also declined from 39.6 per cent in 2023 to 28.79 per cent in 2026, a decrease of approximately 10.9 percentage points. 2. The number of registered voters aged 35–49 increased by 9,852,355, representing an increase of approximately 29.5 per cent. Does this mean young people were removed from the register? Not necessarily. Between 2023 and 2026, three years elapsed. Voters who were aged 32, 33, and 34 in 2023 would have transitioned into the 35–49 age category by 2026. This demographic shift could partially explain the decline in the youth category and the increase in the older age category. Between 2019 and 2023, the register grew to 93,469,008, an increase of 9,464,924 voters (11.27 per cent). By 2026, it had risen further to 103,428,715, representing an additional 9,959,707 voters (10.66 per cent). Although the absolute increase between 2023 and 2026 was slightly higher than that recorded between 2019 and 2023, the percentage growth was marginally lower. These figures demonstrate a declining rate of growth in Nigeria’s voter register: 22.04 per cent in 2015–2019, 11.27 per cent in 2019–2023, and 10.66 per cent in 2023–2026. The most recent period, however, covers three years rather than four. The critical issue, therefore, is not simply whether the voter register is growing, but who is entering the register, how voters are transitioning between age categories, and what these demographic changes mean. My proposal to INEC is to publish a detailed age-cohort analysis explaining changes between the 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2026 registers, including new registrations, age transitions, removal of dead and unqualified persons from the register and other adjustments. If the decline shows inadequate registration among newly eligible young voters, it must prompt increased investment in youth mobilization for voter registration. If it reflects administrative adjustments, those changes must be clearly documented and explained. Samson Itodo is the Executive Director of Yiaga Africa.
